text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes include increased thirst, frequent urination, and ongoing fatigue as cells struggle to get energy from glucose.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and ongoing fatigue

list.snippet: Increased Thirst and Urination: Kidneys work overtime to remove extra sugar, pulling fluids from the body and causing you to go more often and feel very thirsty.
Constant Fatigue: Without enough insulin, glucose cannot enter cells easily, leaving you exhausted even after resting.
Blurred Vision: High blood sugar changes fluid levels, causing the lenses in your eyes to swell and lose focus.
Increased Hunger: Your cells lack energy despite eating, triggering sudden or constant hunger.
Slow-Healing Sores or Cuts: High blood sugar damages blood vessels and lowers your immune response, slowing down wound healing.
Tingling or Numbness: Peripheral nerve damage can start as a mild tingling or loss of feeling in the hands and feet.
Darkened Skin Patches: Acanthosis nigricans causes dark, velvety patches in body folds like the neck, armpits, or groin, signaling insulin resistance.
Frequent Infections: Higher glucose levels make it easier for bacteria and yeast to thrive, leading to recurring skin or urinary tract infections.
